solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Empty Sunday penning paper on bridge rule

indicators.note: penning means holding in, like animals in a pen, so the outer letters wrap round the rest
an empty Sunday has its inside taken out, leaving only the outside letters of the word

parts.note: a quire is a measure of paper, 24 or 25 sheets
an arch is a curved structure spanning a gap, a simple bridge

explanation.surface: A dull, empty Sunday spent writing a paper about a rule of the card game bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' leaves only the ends of Sunday, and 'penning' wraps them round the rest. 'Bridge' suggests the card game but is a curved structure.
explanation.definitionFit: Squirearchy is government or dominance by the landed gentry, a form of rule.

clue.text: Positions over having quit drugs

indicators.note: having quit means the over has left the word for positions

parts.note: stations are posts or positions, as in action stations
O is the cricket abbreviation for over, a set of six balls

explanation.surface: Someone has given up taking drugs and moved on in life.
explanation.definitionFit: Statins are a class of medicines prescribed to lower blood cholesterol.

clue.text: Missing one or two bits at the top, shake organ

indicators.text: Missing one or two bits at the top
indicators.note: the word for shake loses a couple of letters from its start, the top in a down clue

parts.note: to shudder is to shake or tremble

explanation.surface: An instrument with its upper pipes gone gives a trembling sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests the musical instrument but is the milk gland of a cow.
explanation.definitionFit: An udder is the mammary gland of a cow, goat or sheep, a bodily organ.

clue.text: Overwhelming sunlight stifles pale superior in retreat

indicators.note: stifles means smothers, so the sunlight wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a ray is a beam of sunlight

indicators.note: in retreat means going backwards, so the pale superior is read upwards

parts.note: wan means pale
U stands for upper-class or superior, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: Blazing sun smothers a pallid senior figure as he withdraws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In retreat' turns the pale superior back to UNAW, and 'stifles' sets that within the sunlight after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A runaway victory is an overwhelming one, won by a huge margin.

clue.text: Celebrity secrets I lampoon, somewhat upsetting

indicators.note: upsetting says the hidden letters are read backwards
somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A famous figure is somewhat disturbed by a satire exposing their secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upsetting' turns the hidden letters RETSILA upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: An A-lister is a top-rank celebrity, one on the most sought-after guest list.

clue.text: Pest played rock in train

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters within the word for train

parts.note: to coach is to train

indicators.note: played means the letters of rock are performed in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A nuisance played rock music on a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Played' rearranges the fodder to CKRO, which 'in' sets after the second letter of the train word. 'Train' looks like a railway train but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockroaches are scavenging insects that infest kitchens, a classic household pest.

clue.text: Hollow Yorkist victory without local element

indicators.note: a hollow word is emptied of its middle, leaving its outer letters
without means the victory goes without the local

parts.note: a triumph is a victory
PH stands for public house, the local pub

explanation.surface: A Yorkist side wins an empty victory without local support.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is British slang for a neighbourhood pub, and PH is a public house on maps. The Yorkists were one side in England's Wars of the Roses.
explanation.definitionFit: Yttrium is a chemical element, a silvery metal with atomic number 39.

clue.text: Bread eaten by old teacher all the time

indicators.note: something eaten by another goes inside it, so the bread sits within the teacher

parts.note: a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge
naan, also spelt nan, is a flat Indian bread

explanation.surface: An elderly schoolmaster munches bread without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'on and on' means continuously, without ever stopping.

clue.text: Farm animal crossing his building on area in England

parts.note: an ox is a farm animal used for ploughing
a ford is a shallow river crossing

indicators.note: building means the letters of his are put together in a new arrangement

parts.note: re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A beast of burden wanders across a man's building plot in the English countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxfordshire is an English county, with the city of Oxford at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxfordshire is a county in southern central England, so an area of the country.

clue.text: Did work up in Channel Islands start to trouble newsman?

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands, such as Jersey and Guernsey

indicators.note: the start to a word is its first letter, here of trouble

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword newsman

explanation.surface: Was a journalist in Jersey or Guernsey stirred up at the first sign of trouble?
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands are the British islands off the coast of Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite people is to stir or work them up, so the past tense matches 'did work up'.

clue.text: Poet, industrious being at home, shaved amidst junk sadly

indicators.note: amidst means the insect and the home sit inside the rearranged letters
to junk the letters of sadly is to mess them about into another order

parts.note: the ant is proverbially industrious

indicators.note: shaved means the word for home has its last letter trimmed off

explanation.surface: A hard-working poet stays in, clean-shaven, sadly surrounded by rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junk' rearranges the fodder round ANTHOM, the 'shaved' home after the ant. 'Sadly' looks like the anagram signal but is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Dylan Thomas was a Welsh poet, best known for Under Milk Wood.

clue.text: Religious person having spiritual class in remote surroundings

indicators.note: remote surroundings means the word for remote forms a ring around the class

parts.note: far means distant or remote
RI is religious instruction, a school lesson on spiritual matters

explanation.surface: A devout person takes a religious lesson in a far-off setting.
explanation.walkthrough: RI, religious instruction, was the old British name for the school subject now usually called RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A friar is a member of a mendicant religious order, such as a Franciscan.

clue.text: Crusher Bailey perhaps having first spell inside?

indicators.note: inside says the spell and the first go within the wall of the bailey

parts.note: a bailey is the outer wall of a castle, so it is an example of a wall
a term is a spell or period of time
I is the Roman numeral one, so first

explanation.surface: A hard man named Bailey serves his first stretch in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bailey' looks like a person's surname, but a bailey is a castle's outer wall. TERM I reads as term one, the first spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A watermill uses a water wheel to drive millstones that crush grain, so it is a crusher.

clue.text: I run downhill then left through track in a hazardous manner

indicators.note: through means the run and the left pass inside the track's letters

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track
to ski is to run downhill on snow

explanation.surface: A skier describes taking a dangerous run down a slope and veering left across a trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something riskily means doing it with danger, the adverb matching the phrase.

clue.text: English novelist lives with that woman? Hazel possibly

parts.note: is means exists or lives, as in 'while there is life'
her refers to that woman
hazel is one kind of wood, from the hazel tree

explanation.surface: An English writer shares his life with a woman, perhaps called Hazel?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hazel' looks like the woman's name but is the tree and its wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Isherwood was an English novelist, author of Goodbye to Berlin.

clue.text: Bypass repairers maybe wanting settlement — and more

indicators.note: the letters of and more want settling into a proper order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Workers fixing a bypass want a pay deal and something extra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting settlement' reads as a pay dispute but says the letters of AND MORE need settling into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Roadmen are workers who build or mend roads, and a bypass is one kind of road.

clue.text: Exhaust Classical character with constant type of poetry

parts.note: to sap is to drain or exhaust
phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
c is the constant for the speed of light in physics

explanation.surface: Wear out a classic figure who keeps on writing a certain kind of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapphic verse uses a metre named after the Greek poet Sappho of Lesbos.

clue.text: Dated extremely unusual figure in ballet

parts.note: passé means out of date

indicators.note: extremely means taking the extremes, the first and last letters of unusual

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned, very strange figure appears in a ballet.
explanation.definitionFit: A pas seul is a solo dance, a step or figure performed by one dancer in ballet.

clue.text: Criminal, caught with readies regularly, to give up

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of readies

explanation.surface: A villain, nabbed with cash on him time and again, decides to surrender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Readies' is British slang for cash; here only its alternate letters count.
explanation.definitionFit: To concede is to yield or admit defeat, the same as giving up.

clue.text: Jack sorry when speaking about God

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards
eh? is what you say for sorry? when asking someone to repeat themselves

indicators.note: when speaking says the word for about is said aloud and spelt as it sounds

parts.note: over can mean about or concerning, as in a row over money

explanation.surface: A man called Jack apologises while talking about the Almighty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorry' is not an apology but the query 'sorry?', which EH also means. OVER, said in a non-rhotic British accent, comes out as OVAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Jehovah is a name for the God of the Hebrew Bible.

clue.text: Heartless tricks on pensioner, a scapegoat

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word for tricks is taken away

parts.note: jokes are pranks or tricks
OAP is an old-age pensioner

explanation.surface: Cruel pranks are played on an elderly man who gets the blame.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP, old-age pensioner, is the British term for a retired person drawing a state pension.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Soap is British slang for an ordinary dupe who gets the dirty work or the blame, a scapegoat.

clue.text: Gavin and Roz endlessly planned to get one delivered in September?

indicators.note: planned means the letters are arranged into a new design
endlessly means the name Roz loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A couple, Gavin and Roz, timed things so their baby would arrive in autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivered' sounds like childbirth, which is fair: a Virgoan is born roughly from late August to late September.
explanation.definitionFit: A Virgoan is someone born under the star sign Virgo, which covers most of September.

clue.text: Cruise with Ann abroad creating this charge?

indicators.note: abroad in the sense of all over the place, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Taking a cruise overseas with Ann brings a premium to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' fits a holiday surface, where travel cover is a real cost, but signals the anagram of CRUISE and ANN.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurance premium is a charge paid for cover, here against mishaps on the voyage.

clue.text: Hooker's part of this low life hanging around edge of road

indicators.note: hanging around says the low life wraps round the edge of the road

parts.note: scum is a contemptuous word for low-life people

indicators.note: the edge of a word is its first letter, here of road

explanation.surface: A prostitute is one of the lowlife types loitering at the roadside.
explanation.walkthrough: The hooker is not a prostitute but the rugby player who hooks the ball in the scrum, a rugby set piece where the packs bind together and push.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby the hooker binds in the middle of the front row of each pack, so is part of a scrum.

clue.text: Son is going to drink

parts.note: will means is going to, marking the future

explanation.surface: A boy is about to take a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To swill is to drink greedily, gulping in large draughts.

clue.text: Blight overthrowing English flower gutted Yvonne

indicators.note: overthrowing turns the whole string upside down, which in an across clue means reading it backwards

parts.note: a rose is a flower

indicators.note: a gutted word has its insides taken out, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A plant disease topples an English bloom, and Yvonne is devastated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overthrowing' turns back E, ROSE and YE (Yvonne gutted) to give the answer. 'Gutted' looks like Yvonne's feelings but strips her name to its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is an ugly sight that spoils a place, a blight on the landscape.

clue.text: Order, I sense, is threatening

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
nous is common sense or practical intelligence

explanation.surface: Someone who has been given an order says it feels menacing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a British honour awarded by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ominous means boding ill, so it describes something menacing or threatening.

clue.text: Watch display by pioneering German rock band

parts.note: an LED, a light-emitting diode, lights up a digital watch face
Count Ferdinand von Zeppelin pioneered rigid airships

explanation.surface: A digital timepiece readout was made by an innovative German.
explanation.definitionFit: Led Zeppelin were a hugely influential English hard rock group of the 1970s.
